author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Cortex XDR notifications, sent as CEF over syslog from the Cortex cloud tenant. Cortex refuses an internal address, so the notifications go to a data collector or a relay at a public address. Alerts go to the third-party alert schema, and management audit and agent audit logs stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- Cortex XDR sends notifications from its cloud tenant, so the syslog receiver must be reachable from the internet.
- Cortex refuses an internal address, so expose a data collector or a relay at a public address and allow only the Cortex egress addresses for your region, which the syslog receiver page lists.
- Add the receiver under Settings > Configurations > Integrations > External Applications (TCP, UDP or TCP + SSL) and forward alerts to it with a notification forwarding rule.
- Each notification is CEF behind an RFC 5424 header from the host cortexxdr.

Field mapping:
- Alerts from the agent, analytics, BIOC, IOC and correlation rules go to the third-party alert schema, with the event time from end (epoch milliseconds) and severity from the header (6 low, 8 medium, 9 high; Cortex documents no number for critical, so 10 is read as critical).
- Management audit and agent audit logs stay generic.
- Cortex escapes / as \/ in values, and the parser undoes it.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the layout of the alert, management audit and agent audit notification formats.

Testing:
- The child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (95 of 95 fields matched the emulator), and also as a separate parser under its parent (90 of 90 fields).

Known gaps:
- The tenant's built-in PaloAlto_CEF_Master parser matches the same lines and stores them in the generic schema; the engine picks one parser per line, and in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 the built-in parser took the alert lines in 7 of 15 Run Tests and the audit log lines in 8 of 11.
- Expect some lines to keep the built-in mapping.
